_comment: Conformance vectors, generated from the reference synthesiser ITSELF:
https://rgmechex.com/tech/gen1cries.html, driven in headless Chrome over all
151 species with all three channels enabled. `len` is the output length in
samples at 1,048,576 Hz -- the Game Boy's own clock, the rate the reference
computes at -- and `q` is 48 evenly spaced samples of the 8-bit unsigned form
This file exists because every other assertion in check_gen1_apu.mjs compares
the APU against a DESCRIPTION of the reference, and a description can be wrong
in ways that are self-consistent. It was: the length multiplier, the duty
register and the peak normalisation were all wrong, and every one of them
agreed with every other part of this project. Comparing against output is the
only thing that caught them. A tolerance of one 8-bit step is allowed because
this project stores float32 and the reference computes in float64: one ULP is
5.96e-8, which is enough to move an 8-bit sample by one step.
The roster is a 0-indexed array upstream, so dex id is index + 1. Reading it as
pokemon[id] shifts every vector by one species, which produces a plausible
looking file that matches nothing. `cry`/`pitch`/`length` are kept so the
checker can assert the two rosters agree before trusting any of the audio.
